line: Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 Aura Edition (2026, Panther Lake)
config_name: ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 — Core Ultra 7 356H, 32GB LPDDR5, 512GB SSD, 14" WUXGA IPS 500-nit

battery.notes: 58Wh; IPS panel runs ~1.5h longer than OLED per Ultrabookreview IPS-vs-OLED note.

price.notes: IPS tier ~CAD350 below OLED; Lenovo CA.

reviews.quote: Still incredibly compact and light... Battery life is shorter than last year's.
Choosing between the IPS and OLED panels will go on to make a notable difference in runtimes as well.

praises: 500-nit matte IPS is flicker-free and great for all-day spreadsheet work
IPS adds real battery runtime over the OLED tier — best pick for long-haul flights
~980 g: the lightest config of the line
Full ThinkPad port set including HDMI and USB-A, no dongles for office docks
Space Frame repairability: SSD and battery are user-replaceable
complaints: 1920x1200 on a $2,600 laptop feels under-specified next to every rival's 2.8K OLED
60Hz only — scrolling text less smooth than 120Hz OLED tier
IPS contrast is ordinary; blacks grey in dark rooms
Battery still trails last year's Gen 13 despite the efficient panel
Speakers remain weak; most owners use headsets

design_philosophy: The fleet-friendly X1 Carbon tier: matte IPS for flicker-sensitive users and maximum runtime, same Space Frame repairable chassis and 980 g weight as the OLED models.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET/Ultrabookreview Gen 14 OLED review: IPS panel −2.5 screen_quality (1200p/60Hz vs 2.8K 120Hz OLED), +0.5 battery (Ultrabookreview notes IPS runs notably longer), −0.5 productivity (lower res desktop). Image from lenovo.com CA CDN.
